result.result:
The app is built and working, but not to the standard the spec sets. **I never saw the Figma design, and I never used the token resolver.**

- **Figma:** the Figma tool was denied in this session, and the Figma REST API rejected `$FIGMA_ACCESS_TOKEN` as expired. So the layout comes only from the spec's written description, not from the frames. These parts are my guesses:
  - the dashboard arrangement: 4 metric tiles, then the chart spanning two columns next to Service Health and Data Summary, then full-width logs
  - the role badge colours: Admin dark, Editor blue, Viewer grey
  - the brand name "Blueprint Console" and the footer link columns
  - all spacing and proportions
- **Token resolver:** `resolve_token` was denied as well, and I didn't try to reach it any other way. Every token choice was mine, made by reading the descriptions in `public.css` and following `llms.client.txt`. For this arm, that means there is no record of the resolver refusing anything.

**What's verified:** `npx ng build` is clean. A headless-Chrome script ran these flows against `ng serve`, with no console errors:
- The login form shows the required-field errors, `admin`/`admin` reaches `/dashboard`, and `isLoggedIn` is written to `localStorage`.
- The guards redirect correctly in both directions, and unknown URLs redirect as specified.
- The profile menu opens leftward and stays fully on screen (it ends 64px from the right edge at 1280px wide). It closes on an outside click, and Sign Out works.
- Every dialog opens and closes. Edit saves through `PUT`, "Delete user" hands over to the confirmation with the member still selected, delete goes through `DELETE`, invite goes through `POST`, and the delete dialog closes on a backdrop click. The table updated after each change.
- The logs add a line every 3 seconds.

**Token decisions you should know about:**
- **Chart bars:** there is no pure-black token in the public set. I used `--ds-decisions-color-surface-emphasis` (#111), described as the "filled high-contrast surface", and left a comment in `dashboard.component.css`. I didn't use `action-primary-background-active` (#000), because that token means a pressed button, not a chart bar.
- **Fonts:** there is no font-family token, so the page font and the log viewer's monospace font are plain CSS values, each with a comment saying a token is missing.
- **Clean scan:** there are no tier 1 or tier 3 token references and no hex, rgb or hsl colours. The only pixel values are two responsive breakpoints, because CSS doesn't allow variables in media queries.

**Workarounds for library limits:**
- `dsb-header` has no slot for extra content, so the profile control sits on top of it.
- The header and footer links are plain anchors that would reload the page and reset the in-memory data. The layout catches those clicks and sends them through the Angular router instead.
- `dsb-avatar` only shows initials when it's given no image URL at all, so the users page checks each avatar image and clears the URL if it fails to load.
- The read-only fields in the details dialog use disabled `dsb-input`s.

**Setup:** I created the project with Angular CLI 19, which replaced the Angular 21 packages that were preinstalled. I added `angular-in-memory-web-api@^0.19.0`. The code is in `src/app/core`, `layouts/main-layout`, and `pages/{login,dashboard,users}`.

If a working Figma token is provided, the next step is to compare the screens against the frames and fix the dashboard layout, spacing and badge colours.
